Our client is one of the fastest-growing early-stage fintech startups in the US, automating financial operating systems for small businesses. Small businesses deserve the same resources. This role is ideal for someone who wants to be early at a fintech Rocketship, close to product and customers, and have a transformative career experience. We are seeking an AI-Native Software Engineer to help transform our software development process into an AI-first engineering model. In this role, you will use AI tools as a primary development partner to convert requirements into working software solutions faster, while maintaining strong responsibility for quality, correctness, security, and production readiness.
You will be expected to take business and technical requirements, create precise prompts and implementation plans, generate a significant portion of the initial solution using AI, and then carefully validate the output for hallucinations, prompt accuracy, missing logic, incorrect assumptions, and alignment with expected outcomes. The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer with hands-on experience using AI tools for coding, design, testing, documentation, debugging, and refactoring. Use AI-assisted development tools to generate, test, document, refactor, and improve software solutions.
Convert product and business requirements into clear technical prompts, implementation plans, and acceptance criteria.
Generate 80–90% of initial solution drafts using AI tools, then review, validate, and refine the output.
Detect and correct AI hallucinations, inaccurate assumptions, invalid code, security issues, and gaps in requirements.
Create automated tests to verify expected behavior and business outcomes.
Ensure all AI-generated code meets company standards for architecture, security, maintainability, performance, and documentation.
Build reusable prompt templates and AI-native development workflows for common engineering tasks.
Collaborate with product, QA, DevOps, architecture, and security teams to deliver production-ready solutions.
Document prompts, assumptions, validation steps, risks, and final implementation decisions.
Help educate and guide other engineers in adopting AI-native software development practices.

Proficiency in one or more modern programming languages.
Experience using AI coding tools or large language models for software development.
Strong understanding of APIs, databases, cloud services, testing, CI/CD, and secure coding practices.
Ability to write precise prompts and evaluate AI-generated outputs critically.
Strong debugging, testing, code review, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to identify hallucinations, incorrect logic, missing edge cases, and gaps between generated code and requirements.
Excellent communication and documentation skills.
Strong sense of ownership for final deliverables, regardless of whether the initial code was AI-generated.
Education And Experience
Experience with GitHub Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Amazon Q Developer, or similar tools.
Experience creating prompt libraries, AI development workflows, or internal engineering automation.

description_preview:
Own Every Moment at NetApp
At NetApp, your ideas power innovation. We lead in intelligent data infrastructure—delivering unified storage, integrated data services, and solutions that help organizations unlock the full potential of their data, from AI to multicloud.
Ready to innovate and contribute to our path to $10B? Here, you'll collaborate with passionate teams, tackle real-world challenges, and see your impact in how customers transform and grow. If you're ready to bring curiosity, creativity, and drive to every moment, NetApp is where your journey begins. Join teams that innovate to elevate, drive results, and excel together across every function.
Job Summary
We are hiring experienced Systems Software Engineers across multiple NetApp engineering organizations. This pipeline posting is designed to attract strong C/C++ systems-level engineers who can contribute to core storage and data management technologies across ONTAP and other NetApp products. Candidates will be considered for roles on several teams, including ONTAP, WAFL, Replication/HA, Protocols (NFS/SMB/SAN/NVMe), Distributed Systems, Cloud Platforms, and Performance Engineering.
Engineers in these roles design, build, and optimize foundational components of NetApp’s storage stack. You will work on real-world problems involving filesystems, storage internals, distributed systems, performance, scalability, reliability, and data integrity. Work may include developing new features, enhancing subsystems, analyzing complex code paths, improving throughput and latency, debugging customer issues, or driving proofs of concept. You will collaborate with senior engineers, product teams, hardware teams, and cloud engineering groups to deliver high-quality software used globally by enterprise customers.
This posting can support multiple levels (3, 4, and 5). Team and level placement will be determined during the interview process based on experience, technical depth, and demonstrated capabilities.
Job Requirements
Core Responsibilities (All Levels)
Design, implement, and enhance features within ONTAP and related NetApp storage systems
Write high-quality C/C++ code that is efficient, reliable, and maintainable
Analyze and improve existing code paths for performance, scalability, and correctness
Debug complex issues using system-level tools, logs, tracing, and profiling
Collaborate across engineering teams, including filesystem, protocol, cloud, hardware, and QA
Participate in design and code reviews, contributing to engineering best practices
Investigate performance bottlenecks and implement optimizations
Support prototyping, research, and feasibility analysis for new ideas and features
Communicate design decisions, technical findings, and progress clearly with peers
Use AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, development, testing, and troubleshooting
Level‑Specific Requirements
Software Engineer 3 (5–8 years)
Owns well-defined components or features
Implements end-to-end functionality with guidance
Performs profiling, debugging, and testing across subsystems
Contributes to design discussions and supports cross-team integration
Ramps quickly on ONTAP, WAFL, protocols, or storage technologies
Software Engineer 4 (9–15 years)
Designs and owns complex subsystems or multi-sprint epics
Drives cross-team delivery with minimal supervision
Mentors junior and mid-level engineers
Leads deep-dive debugging and performance analysis
Improves reliability, observability, and architecture patterns
Software Engineer 5 (12–16 years)
Leads major technical initiatives across teams or product line
Defines long-term architectural direction and technical strategy
Resolves highly complex system-wide issues in performance, data integrity, HA, scale, or protocols
Mentors senior engineers and influences engineering culture
Demonstrates deep domain expertise in filesystems, operating systems, HA/replication, or distributed systems
Qualifications
Required Technical Qualifications
Strong proficiency in C/C++ for systems-level development
Understanding of data structures, algorithms, memory management, and concurrency
Experience with Unix/Linux systems programming
Experience with one or more: filesystems, storage systems, networking/protocol stacks, distributed systems, high-availability architectures
Strong debugging and performance analysis skills (gdb, perf, tracing, profiling tools)
Ability to write maintainable, well-documented code
Effective communication and collaboration skills
Qualifications that make you stand out:
Experience with ONTAP, WAFL, or similar storage operating systems
Experience with NFS, SMB, SAN (iSCSI/FC), NVMe/TCP, NVMe-oF
Experience with replication, clustering, HA, or consistency protocols
Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI)
Exposure to kernel subsystems, VFS, IO schedulers, caching, or media management
Experience with distributed systems design and large-scale performance tuning
Knowledge of CI/CD, test automation, and modern development practices
Education
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field
Equivalent practical experience considered
Compensation:
The target salary range for this position is $120,000 - $280,000. The salary offered will be determined by the candidate's location, qualifications, experience, and education and may be outside of this range. The range is based on 'On Target Earnings’ (OTE) representing the total potential earnings, which is the sum of the base salary and potential commission earned when performance targets are achieved. Final compensation packages are competitive and in line with industry standards, reflecting a variety of factors, and include a comprehensive benefits package. This may cover Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Retirement or Pension Plans, Paid Time Off, various Leave options, employee stock purchase plan, and/or restricted stocks (RSU’s). These offerings are subject to regional variations and governed by local laws, regula

reason: Stack +11; Title fit +12; Exp fit +6; US +10; Senior desc -30
description_preview:
Location:
New York, NY (Hybrid – 3 days in-office)
One of our hiring partners is looking to hire a 3+ year Full Stack Engineer to join their growing team in NYC. A well-funded, mission-critical startup is taking direct aim at this broken machinery. Backed by Tiger Global and Primary Ventures, this team of healthcare operators, data architects, and product builders is reimagining how provider networks are designed—turning what has historically been a static, compliance-driven exercise into a dynamic, intelligence-driven advantage for payers and patients alike
About the Company:
There is a quiet revolution happening in healthcare, and it is not being waged in a lab or a legislative chamber. It is being fought in spreadsheets, outdated directories, and the manual, error-ridden processes that determine which doctors patients can actually see.
The company already has product-market fit, real customers, and a clear line of sight to massive scale. Now, they are building the engineering team that will take them there.
The Role:
This is not a maintenance role. This is not a ticket-taker role. This is a seat at the table for an engineer with 3+ years of experience who is ready to build like a founder.
The company is seeking a Full Stack Software Engineer to join a small, high-agency team rebuilding the core of their network adequacy platform from the ground up. You will not be siloed to a single view or service. You will touch the entire stack—from React components that shape how customers experience complex data, to Django services that execute the logic determining whether a patient in rural Montana has access to a pediatric endocrinologist.
You will work alongside senior engineers who believe that mentorship is not a distraction from the work, but the work itself. You will have direct access to leadership, clear ownership of meaningful features, and the latitude to make technical decisions that will outlast your tenure.
What You’ll Do:
Own features end-to-end: design, implementation, testing, deployment, and iteration. No handoffs. No ambiguity.
Contribute to the full rewrite of the company’s core adequacy application—modernizing a React frontend and refactoring backend services for scale, performance, and maintainability.
Help scale the company’s adequacy calculations from a single-state prototype to a 50-state enterprise-grade engine.
Partner closely with product, data, and engineering peers to define scope, challenge assumptions, and ship well-architected solutions.
Write code that is clean, tested, and durable—code you would be proud to explain to a future teammate three years from now.
Leverage modern AI tooling not as a crutch, but as a force multiplier, accelerating both velocity and output quality.
Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and the ongoing refinement of how this team builds software.
Who You Are:
You have 3 years of professional full-stack engineering experience. You are past the “learning the ropes” phase and entering the “I can own this” phase.
You are genuinely fluent in modern frontend development. React is your default, not a checkbox.
You have built production software on the backend using a framework like Django, Rails, or equivalent. If that framework is Django, move to the front of the line.
You understand what it means to ship and maintain features in a live production environment—monitoring, debugging, and iterating based on real-world usage.
You are comfortable moving across the stack and hungry to go deeper on both sides.
You are curious about AI-assisted development and have opinions on how to use these tools to write better code, not just more code.
You operate with low ego and high ownership. You ask questions. You admit when you don’t know. You figure it out.
Why Join:
Your impact will be visible.
There is no management layer absorbing scope. You will build things that go directly into the hands of customers who have been waiting for them.
You will be mentored, not managed.
The senior engineers on this team have trained engineers who now lead teams at high-growth startups. They take this seriously.
You will work on genuinely hard problems.
Adequacy is not a CRUD app. It involves complex logic, large datasets, and performance constraints that reward thoughtful architecture.
The mission is real.
This is not healthcare-washing. This is a company fixing a specific, measurable, high-stakes problem that affects millions of Americans.
The team is the perk.
Low politics. High trust. People who would rather ship than argue about who owns what.
Compensation & Benefits:
Meaningful equity ownership—because builders should share in what they build.
Comprehensive health insurance, commuter benefits, and a stipend for home office equipment.
Unlimited PTO, with a team that actually takes it and encourages you to do the same.
A New York City home base with three days per week in-person collaboration. This team likes each other and believes in the signal of face-to-face time.
Location:
New York City (hybrid, 3 days in-office). This role is designed for someone who wants to be part of a physical team, not a distributed one. Remote is not available for this position.

They are live on JWICS, were selected from a field of 200+ companies for a defense innovation challenge and won it, and beat two established defense primes on the same program to earn the follow-on, now in execution.
About the Role
Forward Deployed Engineers build and deploy the company's agentic harness inside customer environments. This platform runs in classified environments across the Intelligence Community and the Department of Defense, and the field organization is structured as small teams embedded at a single customer site for the life of an engagement.
You work directly with analysts and operators to understand what they need, then implement it: connectors against undocumented data sources, agent and integration work against undocumented workflows, and debugging in environments where standard tooling is unavailable.
You report to the lead for your engagement and work alongside the Deployment Strategists on the same team.

The time allocation is published because field engineering is not the same job as platform engineering.
65% engineering: connector and integration development, MCP server construction, platform operation, and troubleshooting in air-gapped environments.
25% users: demonstrations, training, and acting on analyst feedback directly rather than routing it through someone else.
10% feeding the product back: documenting what you learn on site and getting it to core engineering.

Working software in classified customer environments. You build it and you deploy it.
Integrations against customer data sources, including tool development, MCP server construction, and authentication.
Platform operation, so your team's workflows run reliably. You configure agents and workflows in partnership with the Deployment Strategist, who owns whether the output is mission correct.
The user relationship. You demonstrate the platform, deliver training, and act on feedback directly.
Troubleshooting in air-gapped environments where external registries, package managers, and standard debugging tools are unavailable.
Test coverage for error cases, network failures, and disconnected environment edge conditions.
The feedback loop to core engineering. Engagement learnings go back weekly, and they shape the roadmap.
You'll Work Alongside
CIA officers, MIT engineers, Special Operations combat veterans, and applied AI engineers from frontier labs including Anthropic and Google. You will make decisions that immediately affect national security. You will own part of the company early and when it matters.
What This Role Is Not
A deployment role that hands off to someone else for user interaction.
A domain or workflow role without production engineering responsibility.
A role that operates from fully specified requirements.
A remote engineering job with occasional site visits. You sit with your users.

4 to 8 years of professional software engineering experience. Strong Python.
Experience building and operating reliable integrations, including authentication, rate limiting, and error recovery.
Working fluency in Kubernetes and containerized deployment.
Demonstrated experience working directly with non-technical users.
Willingness to work on client site 80 to 100% of the time in the National Capital Region, plus periodic CONUS and OCONUS travel to supported units.
U.S. citizenship and an active TS/SCI clearance.

Experience deploying software in air-gapped or SCIF environments, including disconnected package management and offline container registries.
Prior work with Intelligence Community or DoD tooling, data formats, or workflows in IL6+ environments.
Experience with agentic systems, LLM application development, or evaluation of non-deterministic systems.

Rancher, ArgoCD, or Harbor in restricted environments.

title: Senior Software Engineer (C++)
reason: Title disqualified: Senior Software Engineer (C++)
reject_reason: Title disqualified: Senior Software Engineer (C++)
description_preview:
WHO WE ARE
At Presage Technologies, we believe in improving the quality of healthcare while also making it more affordable and accessible. Over 90% of the world’s population haves access to a device that can power our software, but less than half have access to basic health services. We are aiming to close that gap by developing cutting-edge artificial intelligence and video analytics to transform consumer electronics and mobile phone consumer apps into sophisticated health sensing platforms.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
Our Senior Software Engineer will play a key role in advancing our C++ and Android SDK codebase, while contributing to iOS, Node, and other parts of the stack as needed. You will collaborate closely with our ML Engineers to develop innovative solutions and tackle complex engineering challenges.
Responsibilities include:
Build and extend core SDK functionality in C++ (with JNI for Android integration)
Develop and maintain Android libraries using NDK, Kotlin, and Gradle
Maintain the platform bindings over the C++ core: JNI/Kotlin on Android, Objective-C++/Swift on iOS, and FFI/TypeScript for the Node SDK
Build sample apps and test harnesses across Android, iOS, and Node that prove out SDK integration
Own SDK release engineering: semantic versioning, artifact publishing (Maven Central / SPM / npm), release notes, and migration guides for integrators
Write Python scripts for automation, debugging, and integration with ML pipelines
Profile and optimize C++/Python hot paths alongside our ML Engineers
Raise the engineering bar through code review, test coverage, and CI on a codebase that ships to external developers
This is a hybrid position. Preference will be given to candidates located in the St. Louis, MO; Leesburg, VA; Baltimore, MD metropolitan area; or Minneapolis–Saint Paul (MSP) metropolitan area.
HOW WE BUILD
We’re an AI-native engineering team. Tools like Claude Code and Codex are part of our everyday development workflow, helping us explore, build, and iterate faster.
We do expect you to be excited about using AI effectively while applying strong engineering judgment to the architecture and decisions that matter.
WHO YOU ARE
We expect you to delegate the parts of this job an agent can do. We're hiring for what's left: knowing whether the number coming out of the pipeline is actually right, working out why frame rate collapsed on a mid-range Android device, and making the API decisions we'll live with for the next three years.
Our hardest problems sit where models are weakest, real-time on-device C++, the JNI boundary, the Objective-C++ bridge, camera behavior that differs on every handset, and signal validity where a wrong answer looks exactly like a right one.
You should have:
Modern C++, memory management, cross-platform builds. This is the code where getting it subtly wrong yields a plausible wrong answer rather than a crash.
Experience shipping and maintaining an iOS/Android library or SDK: Swift SPM, Objective-C++, NDK, Kotlin, Gradle, JNI
Fluency with version control, automated testing, and CI/CD
You should also:
Review code you didn't write with real rigor
Know the difference between "the tests pass" and "this is correct," in a domain where ground truth is expensive to obtain
Have debugged problems that don't reproduce under a debugger: device-specific, thermal, timing, memory-over-hours
Have opinions about API surface area, and specifically about what
not
to expose
Nice to have:
TypeScript/Node.js, or another non-mobile binding target (WASM, Python)
Backend or API work: auth, entitlement gating, gRPC/REST services
Applied cryptography or on-device asset protection — Android Keystore, iOS Keychain, signed or encrypted model artifacts
Statistics or signal processing, particularly validating a measurement against expensive ground truth
Regulated software: SaMD, IEC 62304, FDA submissions, or working inside a QMS
INTERVIEW PROCESS
Phase 1: Submit a Resume
Phase 2: Downselection for Introductory Interview with Q&A
Phase 3: Downselection for Performance Task & Technical Interview
Phase 4: Final Interview with CEO and/or CTO
Negotiations and Offer
Timeline:
The entire process can occur in less than two weeks for the right candidate.
Salary Range
$155,000 - $175,000 per year

We are seeking a highly skilled
Data Science Engineer
to build and support advanced machine learning capabilities for Space Domain Awareness (SDA) analytics systems. This role focuses on developing trajectory classification and anomaly detection models, maintaining scalable analytics pipelines, and creating robust evaluation frameworks for sparse, noisy, and incomplete observational data.
The ideal candidate combines strong machine learning expertise with software engineering discipline and has experience working with time-series, state-estimation, or tracking-related systems. You will collaborate closely with astrodynamics, software, and embedded systems teams to ensure models are both scientifically sound and operationally deployable.
What You'll Do
Develop AI/ML models for trajectory classification across orbital regimes and object families.
Build anomaly detection models to identify unusual dynamical behavior and emerging patterns.
Design, integrate, and maintain end-to-end analytical pipelines covering observation processing, orbit estimation, propagation, hypothesis generation, and classification.
Develop benchmarking and evaluation frameworks to assess model accuracy, convergence behavior, false-positive and false-negative rates, confidence calibration, and performance under degraded observation conditions.
Design experiments that validate model generalization through held-out datasets, data degradation studies, and independent benchmark comparisons.
Create calibrated confidence and uncertainty metrics suitable for operational decision-making.
Partner with embedded systems engineers to optimize model size, memory usage, and inference latency for resource-constrained environments.
Implement model optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture simplification.

4+ years of experience developing and deploying machine learning solutions.
Strong proficiency in Python and scientific computing libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas.
Experience with modern deep learning frameworks, preferably PyTorch.
Proven experience building ML systems for time-series, sequential, tracking, or state-estimation-related data.

Experience developing anomaly detection systems for rare-event or weakly labeled datasets.
